notes: Own witness from the read lineage-reads-1985/s-12.json: the reader showed the compiler correct at 85 with its probe (p04b_blank_debug_line_padded.cob), placed as the row's own test with the library texts the reader staged (; run_probe.py could not stage them before kb/Work PB6016, so the import left the row GAP); its expected output is the reader's judged run, equal on this build. The read recorded the kb/Work PB6004 defect (an all-space D line before OBJECT-COMPUTER refused with COBOL7060); PB6004 landed in #1930, and on this build the probe runs and prints its line (re-probed by the rows pass). That a line with D in the indicator area is a debugging line is also VI.4.3@1985-SOURCE-COMPUTER-PARAGRAPH/pb5466-debugging-line-no-mode-parses-both-ways's. The read: 2023 has no debugging lines (GR-6.5-2 discards comment and blank lines, but has no D line). The second sentence makes an all-space debugging line 'the same as a blank line', and 'A blank line can appear anywhere in the source program', so the placement limit for debugging lines (p5) does not reach it. WiseOwl at 85 refuses a D line of spaces between PROGRAM-ID and the ENVIRONMENT DIVISION with COBOL7060 ('A debugging line (indicator D) stands before the end of the OBJECT-COMPUTER paragraph'), both with the line cut at column 7 and padded with spaces to column 72; the same program with a plain blank line runs (BLANK DEBUG LINE ACCEPTED). Code location located after the read: DebuggingLineRewriter.Rewrite classifies the indicator-D lines (comment or source by WITH DEBUGGING MODE) and, since kb/Work PB6004 (#1930), treats a debugging line of spaces from margin A to margin R as a blank line, which may stand anywhere
